title: Speier et al. 2017 — A comparison of stimulus types in online classification of the P300 speller using language models
description: EEG recordings from 10 healthy participants performing an online P300 row-column speller task with a 6x6 character matrix. The study compares two stimulus conditions, Famous Faces and Inverting, using language models for online classification. Data were recorded from 32 channels across two sessions per subject and are distributed in BIDS format with HED event annotations.
methods_description: 32-channel EEG was recorded with a g.tec amplifier at 256 Hz, with a left-ear reference and AFz ground. Participants used a P300 row-column speller with a 125 ms stimulus onset asynchrony and a 25 ms inter-stimulus interval. Each of the 2 sessions per subject had 3 runs, and the visual stimuli were either standard flashes or famous-face overlays.
